Initial commit

WB_Match updated

- Score texts moved to fit the original Pong 1972 more accurately.

Difficulty Selection

- Split Main Menu into two Canvas, MM_GameMode and MM_Difficulty.
- Added three new buttons: Easy_Button, Normal_Button and Hard_Button.
- Changed 1Player behaviour. Instead of changing to Math scene, it hides MM_GameMode and shows MM_Difficulty.
- Created E_Difficulty as a new Enumeration.
- Easy_Button sets GI_MatchInfo Difficuty variable to "Easy".
- Normal_Button sets GI_MatchInfo Difficuty variable to "Normal".
- Hard_Button sets GI_MatchInfo Difficuty variable to "Hard".
- Now, when starting March scene, if 1 Player is selected as the current GameMode, depending on the difficulty selected sets the AISpeed variable with "50.0" if easy is selected, "75.0" if normal is selected or "100.0" if hard is selected.

AI implemented

- When pressing 1Player in the Main Menu, the second player is no longer controlled by keyboard. Instead is controlled through AI.
- AI determines the Ball Y position and moves to that coord vertically.
- AI only determines Ball position when Player 1 collides with the ball or the Ball spawns in direction to Player 2.
- AI moves vertically depending on the AISpeed variable.

Main Menu Updated

- Changed Play_Button to 1Player_Button
- Added 2Player_Button
- Added Quit_Button
- 1Player_Button now changes to Match scene after setting GI_MatchInfo GameMode variable to 0.
- 2Player_Button now changes to Match scene after setting GI_MatchInfo GameMode variable to 1.
- Quit_Button now exits the game.

WB_Endgame Update + Sound Effects

- Create new custom Game Instance called GI_MatchIndo.
- Widget Endgame updates its texts based on GI_MatchInfo.
- Implemented 3 sound effects (SE_Paddle, SE_Wall, SE_Score).
- Now dependeding on the action, a sound effect is played. SE_Wall when the ball collides with the wall, SE_Paddle when the wall collides with a paddle and SE_Score when the wall collides the Player's goal.

HUD changed to Widget

- Changed to enable UI scale adapt to new resolutions
- New font added for player's score

Pong GameMode only in Match level

- Pong GameMode only works in Match level, so Match HUD is only available there.
- Navigation through levels fixed

Match HUD (Scores)

- Implemented 2 Texts that represent both players scores.
- The Texts update with both player's scores.

Match HUD (Middle Line)

- Created Match HUD as a HUD instead of a Widget as it's going to be a non interactive UI.
- Created the middle dashed line to separeate both players.

Created "Current Winner" variable to know last point winner

- When there is a point updates the "Current Winner" variable.
- Depending on "Current Winner" variable, the Ball's initial direction will be left up/down or right up/down.

Based on the Youtube video of the original 1972 Pong, when a player scores a point, the ball will spawn in the direction of the losing player.

Spawning Ball after a point (with delay)

- Now, when a Player makes a point, the ball is destroyed and after 2.7f seconds it is spawned again.

It was necessary an investigation to know about the delay used in the original. Based on a YouTube video of the 1972 Pong, I measured the time spent between a point and the ball's spawn, taking 2.7 as a result.

Spawn Ball and select Initial direction

- Now the Ball spawns at the begining.
- When spawning, it is set a random position in coord Y between (-82, 82)
- When spawning, the Ball selects one of the four different Initial Targets to set its Initial direction.
- There is no longer TargetPoints to set the Ball's Initial direction, now a Vector3D with X (-200 - 200), Y (-200, 200), Z (0) is added to the random spawning position of the Ball. With this addition, the Ball will set a direction of 45º in one of the four different Initial directions selected randomly.

Several changes to match the original Pong 1972

Every object dimension and position has been adjusted to match the original Pong game of 1972

- Paddles, ball, field dimensinos and locations adapted.
- New materials for every object to copy the opriginal ones (some of them are emissive because there is no light).
- Delete level light to create darkness.
- Change camera resolution to 640x480 (4:3, 1.33) SDTV.
- Change camera FOV to 20º and position to show the entire game.

In order to accomplish the objective of creating the original 1972 Pong thers has been an investigation about the original meassures and how to adapt them to UE5.
